themes_detail.label: Electrical Hazards Surge
themes_detail.summary: Electrical complaints in CD310 spiked to 5 reports THIS WEEK compared to a baseline of 0.4 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 1,233% increase (z-score: 6.65)—suggesting either a concentrated infrastructure failure or a wave of unit-level electrical problems affecting resident safety.
evidence: 5 electrical complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (1,233% spike, z-score: 6.65)
Related ELECTRIC category also elevated: 14 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 5.0 avg (180% spike, z-score: 4.99)
Spike is acute and concentrated in current reporting period, not a gradual trend
reporting_angles: Interview Con Edison and NYC Department of Environmental Protection to determine if grid stress, weather damage, or aging infrastructure is driving the spike
Canvas affected blocks to identify if complaints cluster geographically or if residents are experiencing outages, flickering, or fire hazards

themes_detail.label: Door/Window Damage Wave
themes_detail.summary: Door and window complaints jumped to 19 reports LAST WEEK compared to a 5.8 weekly average—a 230% increase (z-score: 4.86)—indicating possible weather damage, break-ins, or building maintenance failures affecting multiple residences.
evidence: 19 door/window complaints last week vs. 5.8 weekly average (230% spike, z-score: 4.86)
Spike is recent and statistically anomalous, not a baseline condition
Potential trigger: recent weather events (snow/ice complaints also elevated in dataset)
reporting_angles: Cross-reference with recent storms or weather events; determine if complaints are weather-related or security-related (break-ins, vandalism)
Interview landlords and property managers to understand repair backlogs and whether complaints indicate systemic maintenance neglect

themes_detail.label: Building Code Violations Explode
themes_detail.summary: Building/Use complaints surged to 61 reports THREE WEEKS AGO compared to a 10.4 weekly average—a 488% increase (z-score: 8.03)—the highest z-score in the dataset, suggesting widespread violations or enforcement activity that warrants immediate investigation.
evidence: 61 building/use complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 10.4 weekly average (488% spike, z-score: 8.03—highest in dataset)
Timing suggests this may be subsiding or may indicate an ongoing enforcement sweep by Department of Buildings
Aligns with CD310's repeated budget requests for DOB capital funding, suggesting chronic building condition issues
reporting_angles: Request DOB data on inspection activity, violation notices, and compliance rates in Bay Ridge/Dyker Heights during the spike period
Interview residents and property owners about what violations triggered complaints (illegal conversions, overcrowding, unsafe conditions, etc.)

themes_detail.label: Dead Animal Reports Triple
themes_detail.summary: Dead animal complaints jumped to 14 reports TWO WEEKS AGO compared to a 2.2 weekly average—a 522% increase (z-score: 4.82)—a public health and sanitation signal that may indicate pest infestation, rodent die-offs from treatment, or environmental contamination.
evidence: 14 dead animal complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 2.2 weekly average (522% spike, z-score: 4.82)
Spike is concentrated in a single reporting period, suggesting acute event rather than baseline condition
CD310 has repeated budget requests for garbage collection and sanitation infrastructure, suggesting systemic service gaps
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Department of Sanitation to determine if the spike correlates with rodent control operations or weather-related animal mortality
Interview residents about observable pest activity and sanitation conditions; investigate whether complaints cluster in specific neighborhoods

themes_detail.label: Street Signage Disappearing
themes_detail.summary: Missing street sign complaints surged to 5 reports THREE WEEKS AGO compared to a 0.8 weekly average—a 567% increase (z-score: 6.43)—indicating either coordinated theft, vandalism, or Department of Transportation maintenance failure.
evidence: 5 missing street sign complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.8 weekly average (567% spike, z-score: 6.43)
Spike is historical (3 weeks old) and may be subsiding; recency is weaker than other leads
Cause unclear: could indicate theft, installation failure, or enforcement sweep of improperly installed signs
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Department of Transportation to determine if signs were removed due to code violations, or if theft/vandalism is occurring
Review incident reports and 311 follow-up data to determine resolution rate and whether signs were replaced
